title: HVAC Software: 7 Tools Compared by the Job They Do
html:
HVAC software works best when you buy it in three layers: field service, books and a way to get found. A service company needs a dispatch and invoicing app, an accounting tool and a free Google Business Profile. Pair them with HVAC SEO so the phone keeps ringing. Published plans in this guide run from $19 to $627 a month, and two vendors publish no price at all.

HVAC software has to do four jobs in a season: book the call, send the right tech, quote the repair and collect payment. Most HVAC owners buy the biggest platform first and then pay for features the office never opens. This guide sorts seven tools by the job each one does. It gives the price each vendor publishes and one real limit for each.

HVAC work swings with the weather. A heat wave or a cold snap can triple the calls in a week, and a slow answer sends the homeowner to the next listing. So the tools below are judged on how they handle a rush. Marketing covers the demand side, and these tools cover the office side. Both have to work together, or the best leads still go cold on a busy Monday.

What HVAC software runs dispatch for a busy service fleet?

ServiceTitan and FieldEdge are the two names fleet owners compare most often. Both are built for trucks, call booking and service agreements, and neither publishes a plan price.

  • ServiceTitan: lists three plans, Starter, Essentials and The Works. Starter covers dispatching, scheduling, call booking, invoicing and a pricebook. Essentials adds mobile estimates and payroll management. Limit: pricing is per technician and quoted on request, so you cannot budget until you book a demo.
  • FieldEdge: lists Select, Premier and Elite plans. Select includes 2 mobile app licenses, Premier 4 and Elite 6. Premier adds multi-option quotes and advanced service agreements. Limit: every plan shows Request Pricing, and the page says no free trial is offered.

Both vendors say pricing depends on team size and add-ons. That is normal for fleet software, but it means you should ask for the full cost in writing. Ask what the per-tech fee covers, what training costs and what happens if you drop a seat in the off season.

Fleet tools also change who does the work. A call booker answers, a dispatcher assigns and techs quote from a tablet, so each role needs training. Budget a few weeks of slower days when you switch, and avoid starting the move in June or January.

A shop with two or three trucks rarely needs this tier. Fleet tools pay off when several dispatchers, memberships and a call center share one board. If you are not there yet, the next group is a better fit.

Which HVAC scheduling software publishes its prices?

Housecall Pro, Service Fusion and Jobber all show dollar prices, so a small HVAC company can plan a budget before a sales call.

  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually for 1 user, or $79 billed monthly. Essentials is $149 annual for 5 users and adds routes, flat-rate pricing and QuickBooks Online sync. Max is $299 annual for 8 users and lists recurring service plans. Limit: extra users on Max cost $35 a month, and add-ons such as Pipeline and Payroll carry no price on the page.
  • Service Fusion: Starter is $208 a month billed annually or $245 month to month. Plus is $325 annual or $382 monthly, and Pro is $533 annual or $627 monthly. Every plan includes unlimited users. Limit: job costing, inventory and a customer portal sit in higher tiers or add-ons, and add-on prices are not listed.
  • Jobber: Core for 1 user is $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 a month billed annually. Extra users on higher plans cost $29 a month each. Limit: card processing is 2.9% plus 30 cents, and add-ons such as Marketing Suite at $99 a month are billed on top.

The cheapest line on a page is not the cheapest bill. An HVAC company with six techs pays per seat on Housecall Pro and Jobber but not on Service Fusion. Price your real headcount on each page before you compare.

Maintenance agreements are where HVAC makes steady money, so look for recurring billing. Housecall Pro lists recurring service plans on Max. Service Fusion lists recurring invoicing on Pro. Check that your plan actually includes it before you sign.

Which accounting software fits an HVAC contractor?

QuickBooks Online is the accounting tool several field service apps sync with, and it lists four plans with monthly prices.

  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start shows $19 a month under a 50% off for 3 months promotion, struck through from $38. Essentials shows $42.50, Plus $70 and Advanced $170 on the same promotion. Simple Start covers 1 user, Essentials 3, Plus 5 and Advanced 25. Limit: the promotion is temporary, so budget for the struck-through price after month three.

Housecall Pro lists QuickBooks Online sync on Essentials. That sync saves double entry of invoices. If your field service app does not sync, expect a weekly hour of manual work at the bookkeeper's desk.

What free tool puts an HVAC company on the map?

Google Business Profile is the free listing that shows your company in Google Maps when a homeowner searches for AC repair nearby. Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge.

  • Google Business Profile: shows your name, service area, phone number, hours and reviews. Limit: it only helps when the address is accurate and the profile gets fresh photos, posts and review replies.

ServiceTitanFleet dispatch and call bookingNot published, per technicianNeeds a demo to price
FieldEdgeDispatch, quotes, service agreementsNot publishedNo free trial listed
Housecall ProScheduling, estimates, payments$59 to $299 a month, billed annuallyAdd-ons not priced
Service FusionScheduling and unlimited users$208 to $533 a month, billed annuallyAdd-ons not priced
JobberQuotes, scheduling, invoices$29 to $49 a month for CoreExtra users cost more
QuickBooks OnlineAccounting$19 to $170 a month on promotionPromotion ends after 3 months
Google Business ProfileMap listingFreeNeeds steady upkeep

How much does HVAC software cost for a six-tech shop?

A six-tech HVAC shop on Service Fusion Starter pays $208 a month billed annually, because every plan includes unlimited users. Add QuickBooks Essentials at its struck-through price of $85, and the monthly software bill is about $293 before processing fees.

The same shop on Housecall Pro needs a plan that covers six users. Essentials lists 5 users at $149 billed annually, and its page does not price a sixth seat. Max lists 8 users at $299 billed annually. Add the same QuickBooks plan and the bill is about $384.

Neither number includes card processing. Housecall Pro says rates start as low as 2.59%, and Jobber lists 2.9% plus 30 cents. On a sample $9,000 system replacement, one percentage point is $90. Ask every vendor for the rate on your average ticket, because that fee can outweigh the plan price.

These are list prices from each vendor's page, not quotes. Annual billing is paid up front, and Jobber states that its initial annual payment is non-refundable. Month-to-month billing costs more per month but lets you leave after a bad summer.

What should you ask before you sign for HVAC software?

Ask five questions in the demo and write down the answers. Vendors change plans often, so the written answer matters more than the page you read today.

Run a rush-day test during the free trial if one exists. Book ten fake calls in one hour, reroute two techs and send three quotes. Housecall Pro lists a 14-day trial on Max, and Jobber lists a 14-day trial of Grow. If the app slows the office down in the test, it will slow you down in July.

What does HVAC software not do for you?

HVAC software organizes the work you already have. It does not create demand, and none of the tools above writes a service page, ranks a website or runs an ad.

Demand comes from search and maps. Organic rankings take longer but keep working after the spend stops.

Your website is the other half. A booking form that writes into your field service app saves a phone call.

How do you choose HVAC software for your company?

Choose HVAC software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it handle maintenance agreements, flat-rate pricing and multi-option quotes, or only one-off jobs?

Cost: add the plan price, extra seats, card processing fees and add-ons, then compare the total to one average repair ticket.

Setup effort: can the office import customers and a pricebook in a week, or does it need paid onboarding?

A one-truck owner can run on Housecall Pro Basic or Jobber Core, QuickBooks Simple Start and a free Google Business Profile. That stack costs about $100 a month at list prices, before processing fees.

A shop with five to ten techs fits Service Fusion with unlimited users, or Housecall Pro Essentials or Max. Add QuickBooks Plus and a managed local SEO plan. A multi-truck company with dispatchers and a call center should book demos with ServiceTitan and FieldEdge and compare their written quotes.

Software works hardest when leads keep coming. The HVAC CRM automation service connects follow-up to the tools above.

For a similar service trade, read the garage door software guide.

What software does an HVAC company need?

An HVAC company needs a field service app for booking, dispatch, quotes and invoices. It also needs accounting software and a Google Business Profile so homeowners can find it. Start with job management, then add maintenance agreement billing once repeat customers make up a large share of your work.

How much does HVAC software cost?

Published plans here run from $19 a month for promotional QuickBooks Simple Start to $627 for Service Fusion Pro billed monthly. ServiceTitan and FieldEdge publish no price. Processing fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so confirm the total for your headcount with each vendor.

Is Housecall Pro or Jobber better for an HVAC company?

Both cover scheduling, estimates, invoices and payments, so team size and add-ons decide it. Housecall Pro lists 1 user at $59 a month billed annually. Jobber lists Core for 1 user at $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 billed annually.

Does HVAC software include maintenance agreement billing?

Some plans do. Housecall Pro lists recurring service plans on its Max plan, and Service Fusion lists recurring invoicing on Pro. FieldEdge lists basic service agreements on Select and advanced ones on Premier and Elite. Confirm the exact feature on your plan before you sign.

Is ServiceTitan worth it for a small HVAC company?

ServiceTitan publishes no prices and quotes per technician, so a small shop cannot judge the cost without a demo. It is built for fleets with dispatchers and call booking. A company with one or two trucks usually does better starting with a lower cost app.

Is Google Business Profile free for an HVAC company?

Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: accurate service areas, photos of finished installs and replies to every review. Google's paid ad products, such as Local Service Ads, are separate.

What should a new HVAC company buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a simple website first, because calls come before dispatch. Then add one field service app that fits your headcount. Add accounting sync once invoices pile up. Skip fleet platforms until several trucks share one board.

###
What software does an HVAC company need?
An HVAC company needs a field service app for booking, dispatch, quotes and invoices. It also needs accounting software and a Google Business Profile so homeowners can find it. Start with job management, then add maintenance agreement billing once repeat customers make up a large share of your work.
###
How much does HVAC software cost?
Published plans here run from $19 a month for promotional QuickBooks Simple Start to $627 for Service Fusion Pro billed monthly. ServiceTitan and FieldEdge publish no price. Processing fees, extra users and add-ons cost more, so confirm the total for your headcount with each vendor.
###
Is Housecall Pro or Jobber better for an HVAC company?
Both cover scheduling, estimates, invoices and payments, so team size and add-ons decide it. Housecall Pro lists 1 user at $59 a month billed annually. Jobber lists Core for 1 user at $49 a month with no commitment, or $29 billed annually.
###
Does HVAC software include maintenance agreement billing?
Some plans do. Housecall Pro lists recurring service plans on its Max plan, and Service Fusion lists recurring invoicing on Pro. FieldEdge lists basic service agreements on Select and advanced ones on Premier and Elite. Confirm the exact feature on your plan before you sign.
###
Is ServiceTitan worth it for a small HVAC company?
ServiceTitan publishes no prices and quotes per technician, so a small shop cannot judge the cost without a demo. It is built for fleets with dispatchers and call booking. A company with one or two trucks usually does better starting with a lower cost app.
###
Is Google Business Profile free for an HVAC company?
Google states that you can add or claim your business at no charge. It still takes work: accurate service areas, photos of finished installs and replies to every review. Google's paid ad products, such as Local Service Ads, are separate.
###
What should a new HVAC company buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and a simple website first, because calls come before dispatch. Then add one field service app that fits your headcount. Add accounting sync once invoices pile up. Skip fleet platforms until several trucks share one board.
